introduction: ERC-5568 defines a machine-readable format that lets a smart contract tell a wallet the user must take an action, such as approving a token, before a transaction succeeds. It was proposed by Gavin John in August 2022. A contract exposes a well-known walletSignal24 view function that returns an instruction_id and instruction_data, or reverts with a WalletSignal24 error, and the wallet simulates the call and resolves it. Note: ERC-5568 is in Review status; the interface may still change before it is finalized.
designPurpose: ERC-5568 was designed to move action-signaling logic out of hard-coded front-end code and into the contract itself. Before it, a dApp interface had to know that a call would fail without, say, a prior token approval, and encode that recovery flow by hand for every contract. ERC-5568 lets the contract declare the needed action through one well-known function and a reserved revert error, so any wallet can detect and resolve it generically, carrying an instruction id plus up to 64 kB of arbitrary parameters.
commonUsage: The format targets wallets and the contracts they interact with: an exchange can ask the wallet to approve a token before a trade, request an off-chain HTTP request, or prompt the user to rotate keys on a schedule. Because an instruction id is namespaced to the ERC number that defines it, other standards can add new instruction types that any ERC-5568-aware wallet understands. As a Review-stage proposal, it is mainly of interest to wallet developers and standards authors.
fn.walletSignal24.desc: A well-known view function a wallet simulates before broadcasting a transaction. It returns a nonzero instruction_id with instruction_data when the user must act, or an instruction_id of 0 when no action is needed.
fn.walletSignal24.params.selector: A selector identifying the operation the wallet intends to perform.
fn.walletSignal24.params.function_data: Arbitrary calldata describing the intended operation, letting the contract decide which instruction to return.
fn.walletSignal24.returns.instruction_id: The instruction identifier, equal to the ERC number of the required action, or 0 when no action is needed.
fn.walletSignal24.returns.instruction_da: Up to 64 kB of instruction parameters, whose structure is defined by the ERC that owns the instruction_id.
sim.walletSignalWalkthrough.name: Wallet Signal Walkthrough
sim.walletSignalWalkthrough.desc: Follow how a contract signals a required action to a wallet through walletSignal24 and the WalletSignal24 error.
sim.walletSignalWalkthrough.step.call: The wallet simulates walletSignal24 on the contract before broadcasting the user's transaction.
sim.walletSignalWalkthrough.step.execute: The contract determines that an action is required and returns a nonzero instruction_id, or reverts with the WalletSignal24 error carrying the same data.
sim.walletSignalWalkthrough.step.signal: The wallet parses the instruction, prompts the user to complete the required action, then re-evaluates the original transaction.
